observations: Photo 0 shows a black PlayStation 4 console with a purple and black controller resting on top.
The console has a visible Mario sticker on the left side and some scratches and wear on the surface.
The right side of the console clearly shows 'PS4' branding.
The console appears to be a standard model, not a slim or Pro variant, based on its thickness and design.
The controller is not a standard PS4 DualShock; it has a purple color scheme and a different button layout, possibly a third-party or modified controller.
The seller claims the console is 'hacked with action games', but no evidence of hacking or installed games is visible in the photo.

claims.claim: It is hacked with action games
claims.evidence: No screen or interface is shown to verify the hacking or installed games. The claim cannot be confirmed from the photo alone.

risks.risk: The console may be a counterfeit or non-genuine unit.
risks.proof: A close-up of the serial number and model label on the back of the console, along with a video of the console booting up with the official Sony logo.

risks.risk: The controller may be non-functional or incompatible with the console.
risks.proof: A video showing the controller connecting to the console and being used to navigate the menu or play a game.

risks.risk: The 'hacking' claim may be false or misleading, and the console may not have any games installed.
risks.proof: A screenshot or video of the console's home screen showing installed games or a modded interface.

proof_requests: Video of the console powering on and booting up.
Video of the controller connecting and being used to navigate the console.
Screenshot or video of the console's home screen showing installed games or modded interface.

response.reason: The console is identifiable as a PS4, but the claim of being 'hacked with action games' cannot be verified from the photo. Multiple risks exist regarding functionality, authenticity, and the controller's compatibility. Proof is needed to assess the true condition and value.
